notes: Continuity ledger for the daily research workflow (spec/RESEARCH_BRIEF.md). The agent reads this before researching and updates it after filing the day report. Hand-correctable at any time — this file wins over prose in dossiers.

counters.cumulativeTargetsNote: Last quantified by CENTCOM Jul 11; treat as floor, only raise with a new official cumulative figure. No-strikes streak of 30 ended Aug 30 with confirmed US strikes on Larak Island (NIGHT 01), rebuilt to 1 after a strike-free Aug 31, then RESET to 0 on Sep 1 — confirmed US strikes inside Iran (~100 targets across southern Iran per Axios, single-chain; CENTCOM confirmed the barrage 'completed': air defenses, radar, maritime assets, mine-laying, communications) open NIGHT 02 and resume the consecutive-strike campaign. Axios's ~100-target figure is single-chain reporting, not an official cumulative. WaPo reports fighting 'likely to remain limited,' with Patriot-interceptor depletion cited as a re-escalation constraint; the Sep 1 exchange is the biggest since July — watch for a NIGHT 03.

blockadeLedger.note: CENTCOM maritime interdiction accounting, carried in dossiers since the pause. Last confirmed accounting remains Aug 30 via CENTCOM X post ('as of Aug. 30', 9:16 PM ET), corroborated verbatim by gCaptain. No CENTCOM tally with a confirmable 'as of Sep 1' label was found in any fetched source; The Peninsula's 84/3/2 ('announced Tuesday' per QNA, published Sep 1 18:38 UTC) quotes no 'as of' label — post-window approximate, adopt only if a primary CENTCOM post or second outlet confirms it. Sep 1 additions: two laden tankers hit by unidentified projectiles overnight Aug 31→Sep 1 (SIDR + Senegal Prosperity; second name single-chain; no attribution; no UKMTO bulletin in-window), and CENTCOM cited Tehran's 'overnight attacks on ships transiting' the strait as part of the strike wave's trigger. Counts-vs-claims fight unreconciled: US officials per Axios say 15–20 tankers/night through the southern corridor (~10M bpd, ~half prewar volume) vs Kpler's preliminary five Monday vessels (no liquid tankers) vs Trump's 'averaging 30 ships a night'; Energy Sec Wright: >17M barrels exited Aug 31. INTERTANKO (Sep 1): TSS mine clearance 'a necessary condition… not sufficient on its own'.

openThreads.text: Upcoming Xi–Trump meeting complicates secondary-sanctions action against Chinese banks. Updated Aug 27: Trump coy in the Oval Office — 'Who said I'm not? You don't know if I'm doing it' — but no major Chinese financial institution has been listed. Updated Aug 30: Bessent pushed back on China-bank critics — the blockade has already curbed most of China's Iran oil purchases and Iranian oil in floating storage is dwindling ('Problem solved'); still no Chinese institution listed, and the new weekly bank-first sanctions cadence keeps the question live. Updated Aug 31: Bessent at the G20 in Asheville — Outcast 'can work without China'; met PBoC Governor Pan Gongsheng Sunday ('more in common with the Chinese on Iran than we disagree on'; per AP 'all options are on the table' on Beijing's continued Iranian oil purchases); still no Chinese institution listed. Updated Sep 1: G20 finance meeting closed with no joint communiqué — China the lone holdout, objecting to four sections including one on the Strait of Hormuz and ongoing wars; the US issued a chair's statement agreed by all members except China. Bessent vowed to 'economically asphyxiate this regime' — IRGC offshore accounts in the British Virgin Islands and '$100 million houses… We are going to freeze those' — and per Reuters Washington is eyeing airlines, the maritime industry and digital assets next. Still no Chinese institution listed; bank sanctions 'expected to start this week'.
Bessent predicts a 'broad array' of countries follows UAE in cutting trade ties — watch for named countries.
Iran threatened to halt all oil exports in response to the sanctions campaign.

Tanker strikes in the strait: week's third commercial-vessel strike — Saturday Aug 29 an unknown projectile hit a tanker 12nm north of al-Khasab, Oman (no injuries or environmental damage; UKMTO warning issued late Sunday — delayed reporting; no attribution, no Iranian claim or denial). Prior items: Monday's Ash Shishah vessel name still unconfirmed (UKMTO 120-26, Liberian-flagged per Fox); Kuwaiti-connected tanker's tow/salvage status unchanged; Kuwait separately told the IMO a KPC supertanker was struck earlier in August. UKMTO Aug 29: strait risk SEVERE, traffic 'significantly reduced,' operators favouring the Northern route, continuing IRGC harassment (drone overflights, targeted surveillance of merchant vessels, radio transmissions). Watch attribution, tow/salvage status, and UKMTO follow-ups. Updated Aug 30: UKMTO WARNING 122-26 (issued Sunday, 4:22 PM) formalizes the Saturday strike — 'unknown projectile' while inbound 12nm north of Khasab, no casualties or environmental impact, investigation underway, third UKMTO-reported attack in a week; still no attribution and no tow/salvage update. Updated Aug 31: IRGC/state TV claimed a supertanker struck two naval mines on the southern route and stopped/burned — vessel never named; CENTCOM: 'This is FALSE. No ships have hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz… another IRGC attempt to intimidate regional commercial shipping through disinformation'; no UKMTO confirmation on Aug 31. Then late Aug 31 Bahri's tanker SIDR was hit in a 'security incident' transiting the strait — two Filipino seafarers killed, the tanker-strike sequence's first confirmed commercial-vessel fatalities (operator confirmation Sep 2; Marisks had reported 'unknown projectiles' on two tankers overnight Aug 31→Sep 1); attribution unclaimed; aftermath tracked in its own thread. Prior strikes' tow/salvage status unchanged. Updated Sep 1: two MORE laden tankers hit by unidentified projectiles within minutes of each other overnight Aug 31→Sep 1 — the Saudi-flagged SIDR (aftermath in its own thread) and the Liberian-flagged Senegal Prosperity (name single-chain via Newsmax citing shipping-intelligence/vessel-tracking firms), both carrying Saudi crude; no attribution claimed and no UKMTO bulletin captured in-window. CENTCOM cited Tehran's 'overnight attacks on ships transiting' the strait and 'recent attempted attacks' on shipping and US service members as part of the strike wave's trigger. Prior strikes' tow/salvage status unchanged.

Pakistan mediation round one (Munir's Tehran visit) closed without visible outcome. Updated Aug 29: Gharibabadi framed the weekend's Qatari and Pakistani visits as aimed at determining whether the parties can return to implementing the Islamabad MoU's commitments; Qatar remains the visible mediation channel — watch for a second round, a concrete next step, or US engagement on the MoU. Updated Aug 31: no second round; Pezeshkian at SCO Bishkek — the US 'has not fulfilled its commitments' and 'there are currents within America that see their interests in the continuation of war.' Updated Sep 1: PM Sharif met Pezeshkian on the SCO Bishkek sidelines — Islamabad says it 'remains engaged' with both sides; still no visible mediation round or concrete next step.

Iran–Oman Hormuz corridor — first 'reached' claim: Gharibabadi said Aug 29 Iran and Oman have reached an understanding over the strait, but it 'will not be implemented until the United States fulfills its commitments under the Islamabad MoU'; 'the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, and any vessel passing through the strait does so in coordination with Iran'; Tehran will continue 'defensive measures' and is 'prepared for any scenario.' Pezeshkian separately urged reviving the lapsed June 17 MoU (~90M barrels sold under it). Still unresolved: the transit-fee dispute, the 30–60-day permanent-scheme negotiation, Rezaei's 'designated central channel' conditional on the US first meeting Iran's conditions, and White House non-engagement — watch for implementation, US reaction, IMO notification, and corridor usage data. Updated Aug 31: Gharibabadi proposal terms re-detailed (inbound through Iranian waters, no military vessels ever, 60-day permanent-scheme negotiation); deadlock framing stands — Trump demands the strait reopen before talks, Iran demands the US halt its campaign first. Updated Sep 1: Pezeshkian at Bishkek offered immediate reciprocity — 'If the U.S. returns to its commitments in the memorandum of understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately reciprocate'; the IRGC said the US strikes had only 'tightened' Iran's effective closure of the strait; INTERTANKO notes Iran still insists vessels use its northern corridor. No implementation, US reaction, IMO notification or corridor-usage news; deadlock framing stands.

Pezeshkian–Putin meeting at SCO Bishkek (Sept 1) incl. a reported $25B nuclear-plants MOU — watch for outcomes. Updated Sep 1: meeting held — Putin pledged Russia is 'striving to provide you with the necessary assistance… supplying you with essential goods' and lamented the 'unstable and all too fragile' June truce (Kremlin readout via WaPo); the SCO joint statement condemned 'military strikes on the territory of the Islamic Republic of Iran, which have resulted in numerous civilian casualties' and opposed 'unilateral coercive measures.' The reported $25B nuclear-plants MOU remains unconfirmed by any fetched Sep 1 coverage (report dates to Aug 28) — watch for confirmation.
NBC intel-damage report (≥20 US government sites in 8 countries, 2,000+ projectiles, CIA station Riyadh hit, billions in repairs) — watch for official confirmation/denial or the original NBC filing.

Southern-route friction: no new enforcement incident Aug 27; Cooper reports mines cleared, international lanes open, 'momentum building' (~1,500 vessels assisted, ~750M barrels protected) while Kpler counted only 5 transits vs traders' ~7–8M bpd exiting (dark/shuttle trade gap); prior items — Iranian warship deterring HAANA from the southern 'Oman corridor', Saudi STS supertankers off Oman, Trump's 'immediately and systematically destroyed' warning to new mine-layers — remain watch items; track enforcement incidents and corridor usage. Updated Aug 30: Kpler counted 5 visible transits/day over the weekend (Friday 14 incl. a dark VLCC laden with 2M bbl Qatari crude); TankerTrackers averaged ~6.7M bpd crude passing the blockade line over the past 7 days (single tracker, AIS + satellite); the Larak strike followed US intel that the IRGC was preparing to fire mine-carrying rockets into the strait, days after CENTCOM's mine clearance; INTERTANKO 'not sufficient' warning lands Sep 1. Updated Aug 31: Trump — strait 'in extremely good shape', 'we've been averaging 30 ships a night' with Navy assistance (escort claim tracked as its own thread against transit counts); CENTCOM's Hawkins: 'US forces are monitoring the area closely and remain prepared to protect the free flow of commerce'; UBS: the US–Venezuela deal has 'little immediate impact' on crude or US gasoline — the weekend's fighting offset its supply-hope bump. Updated Sep 1: INTERTANKO's warning landed — TSS mine clearance is 'a necessary condition… not sufficient on its own' (Iran still insists on its northern corridor; JMIC still warns of drifting/uncharted mines; Treasury has warned against three Iranian-linked safe-passage-fee entities). Counts fight widened: US officials per Axios say 15–20 tankers/night through the southern corridor on many nights (~10M bpd, roughly half prewar volume) vs Kpler's preliminary five Monday vessels with no liquid tankers among them; Energy Sec Wright: >17M barrels exited the strait Aug 31. The mines-vs-projectiles dispute is now a CENTCOM-vs-IRGC information war.

Rezaei compiling Iran's formal conditions list for reopening Hormuz: reportedly up to $300B compensation for wartime damages, removal of US sanctions, ~$100B frozen assets released, end to the regional war, lifting of the naval blockade (exact sums single-outlet via Crypto Briefing; wires confirm the list itself) — watch for the formal list, US response, and whether the 'designated central channel' opens.

DOJ reviving maritime prize courts to condemn and sell vessels/cargo seized enforcing the blockade, proceeds to Treasury (Bloomberg via Fox Business; SD Tex US Attorney Reitz) — watch for the first condemnation filings and expected owner legal challenges.

FinCEN's Banque Misr UAE special measure is an NPRM (UAE-branch scope only; Egyptian parent untouched). Updated Aug 29: Banque Misr says it is reviewing the notice 'with utmost seriousness and attention' while its UAE branches keep serving customers; Egypt's central bank says it and the foreign ministry are in contact with US officials, noting the measure is limited to Banque Misr UAE's USD transactions with correspondent banks. Forbes (Aug 30, post-window): Federal Register publication had not yet appeared — the 30-day comment clock had not started. Watch for Federal Register publication, finalization, and further Egyptian/UAE central-bank responses to the proposed correspondent-account cutoff. Updated Aug 31: UAE central bank ordered a 'special and urgent examination' — a forensic lookback over the two-year period Treasury cited — and is weighing the bank's status if the US measure takes effect; Bessent: measures deliberately stop at the branches — 'We did not impose sanctions because we did not want the measures to extend to the parent Banque Misr' (Section 311 invoked, 'never engaged in an action at this level of force'); comment period runs to Oct 1, 2026 — the Federal Register clock has started, updating the Aug 29 Forbes note.

US–Venezuela oil deal implementation: 17 fields, >65B barrels in associated reserves, 55% effective US output share, 100-year rights, ~$100B promised private investment — watch SPR replenishment purchases, the reported Venezuela OPEC exit, and legal/constitutional challenges (Democrats opposed). Updated Aug 30: Trump said SPR 'topping out' with oil secured under the deal 'will begin shortly' — 'Gift from Venezuela to the People of the United States'; reserve ~290M bbl as of Aug 21 (near 44-year low, fell ~3.1M bbl the prior week); delivery timing and pump relief unclear. Updated Aug 31: Chevron, ONGC, GE Vernova, Eni and GeoPark are on track to sign final agreements 'as early as this week' (Reuters, five sources; signings post-window — tracked as a new thread); Trump: Exxon and Chevron among companies 'committed to invest'; pact covers 17 fields with ~64B bbl proved reserves per Reuters (earlier White House framing >65B — attribute per outlet), 1.5M bpd long-term vs 1.25M bpd now; Vance confirms 'a significant increase in oil production out of Venezuela.' Updated Sep 1: at the Cabinet Room refiners meeting Trump asked how to process more Venezuelan crude; participants praised the Jones Act waiver. Post-window Sep 2: Chevron signed — $7B investment, two more Orinoco fields, production to 600K bpd by 2031 from ~280K (CNBC); NABEP has granted the DoD a 35% equity stake; Energy Sec Wright visiting Venezuela Wednesday. Resolves the 'Venezuela pact signings this week' thread; SPR replenishment purchases and the reported Venezuela OPEC exit remain open.

Weekly secondary-sanctions cadence: Bessent — 'You're going to see a lot more of these every week', banks first, with possible escalation to cutting an institution off entirely from the dollar system ('There can be no leakage'); first package of the new rhythm expected week of Aug 31; G20 Asheville finance meeting Aug 31–Sep 1. Updated Aug 31: no new designations landed Aug 31; Bessent at G20 — another Iranian bank this week, one more the following week, aircraft-leasing measures under consideration; G20 day one held (NYT/WSJ/Bloomberg reporters barred); European Commission 'welcomes' economic pressure 'including through the US-led Operation Economic Outcast.' Updated Sep 1: no new designations landed; the G20 finance meeting closed without a communiqué (China lone holdout on four sections incl. Hormuz/wars; US chair's statement agreed by all but China) and bank sanctions are 'expected to start this week'; per Reuters Washington is eyeing airlines, the maritime industry and digital assets as the next pressure targets; Bessent vowed to 'economically asphyxiate this regime' and freeze IRGC offshore accounts.

Larak casualty figures — 3 killed per Tasnim, two IRGC Navy per Nournews — Iranian-side only; watch for independent tolls or official confirmation. Updated Aug 31: IRNA citing Qeshm County Gov. Hossein Amirtaymouri — 'at least two people were killed and several others wounded'; a third Iranian-side variant (Tasnim 3 / Nournews 2 IRGC Navy / IRNA ≥2); still no independent toll.

WaPo Hegseth leak — force sustainability: in the classified Aug 14 Secretary of Defense Orders Book, the EUCOM, PACOM and SOUTHCOM commanders and CNO Adm. Daryl Caudle filed formal 'non-concurs' against orders keeping 50,000+ troops in the Middle East through September, some into 2027 — Caudle: the Navy 'cannot sustain' the current level with barely one-fourth of the destroyer fleet ready to deploy; Patriot-interceptor depletion is limiting the administration's ability to re-escalate; elements of the 82nd Airborne see tours extended to a year (commander's letter dated Aug 30). Pentagon spokesman Parnell did not dispute the objections — 'Non-concurs are standard' — while warning that publishing the orders book 'is a crime.' Story Aug 30-dated, surfaced in Aug 31 coverage. Watch: follow-up reporting, official responses, whether the posture actually extends, and any open civil-military friction over the campaign. Updated Sep 1: Army Secretary Driscoll's exit went public — his first statement since the White House confirmation came late Tuesday on X ('the honor of a lifetime,' no reason given, praise for Hegseth), Wednesday his last full day; the Army is left without Senate-confirmed civilian or uniformed leaders as strikes resume. Bipartisan criticism: Tillis urged Trump to 'find a new leader at the Pentagon who will retain and empower our military talent'; Reed accused Hegseth of 'cultivating a culture where dissent is punished'; Rounds predicted 'serious questions' when senators return.

SIDR aftermath: Bahri's tanker SIDR was attacked late Aug 31 transiting the Strait of Hormuz — two Filipino seafarers killed, the tanker-strike sequence's first confirmed commercial-vessel fatalities (Bahri statement confirmed Sep 2 via X; Straits Times/AFP/Reuters + Argaam). Attribution unclaimed — Bahri says only 'security incident'; Marisks reported 'unknown projectiles' on two tankers overnight Aug 31→Sep 1 (both laden with 2M bbl Saudi crude at Juaymah per Kpler; second tanker unnamed/unconfirmed); CENTCOM's same-day 'No ships have hit mines' denial addresses mines, not projectiles, and predates the confirmation. Watch: attribution, the second tanker's identity, UKMTO confirmation, whether CENTCOM/UKMTO address SIDR, casualty/salvage follow-up, Bahri and industry response, insurance-market reaction. Updated Sep 1: the second overnight tanker is named — Liberian-flagged Senegal Prosperity (Newsmax citing shipping-intelligence/vessel-tracking firms; single-chain); CENTCOM cited Tehran's 'overnight attacks on ships transiting' the strait as part of the strike wave's trigger, but no CENTCOM or UKMTO statement addressing SIDR specifically was found in fetched sources; attribution still unclaimed. Post-window Sep 2: Philippine Migrant Workers Secretary Cacdac — the two killed seafarers' remains and 14 survivors to be flown home, ~3,000 Filipino seafarers still in the Gulf; Saudi MOFA condemned the attack and urged a return to negotiations.

Trump's 'averaging 30 ships a night' escort claim vs transit counts: Trump says the Navy has been 'averaging 30 ships a night' escorting strait traffic and the strait is in 'extremely good shape' — vs Kpler's ~5 visible transits/day (Aug 30 data) and TankerTrackers' ~6.7M bpd past the blockade line. Reconcile against the next transit counts and CENTCOM accounting. Updated Sep 1: still unreconciled — new US-side datapoints (Axios: US officials say 15–20 tankers/night through the southern corridor on many nights, ~10M bpd roughly half prewar volume; Energy Sec Wright: >17M barrels exited the strait Aug 31) vs Kpler's preliminary five Monday vessels with no liquid tankers among them; CENTCOM ledger unchanged with no 'as of Sep 1' label.

US 'tanker-for-tanker' turn: Axios (single-chain) reports US forces struck two Iranian government tankers in their engine rooms off Iran's coast north of the blockade line — direct retaliation for attacks on shipping — within the ~100-target Sep 1 strike wave. Watch official confirmation or denial, Iranian retaliation against commercial shipping (tit-for-tat tanker warfare), and war-risk insurance reaction.

Kuhestak wedding-strike fallout: a US strike hit a home hosting a wedding in Kuhestak (Sirik County) on the coast overlooking the strait — tolls contested and revised (5 killed incl. a child per deputy Gov. Nafisi → 4: two women, two children aged 4 and 16, no explanation; wounded ≥63–68; Reuters could not independently verify); CENTCOM: 'The U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC.' Iranian officials liken it to the war's first-night girls'-school strike (160 killed; Pentagon probe findings never released) — watch independent verification, 'war crime' framing, and whether it drives further escalation or Gulf opinion.
FT report (via CNBC): Russia secretly helping Iran develop supersonic anti-ship cruise missiles threatening US carriers — single-chain, likely Sep 2-dated; verify the original filing and follow-ups.

Gulf-states exposure: Kuwait hit directly (Ali Al Salem airbase missile-and-drone attack, drone-started residential blaze) and called the attacks 'criminal Iranian aggression'; Qatar said it holds Iran responsible for the attacks and their repercussions; the Council of Arab Interior Ministers condemned attacks on Kuwait, Jordan, UAE and Bahrain as a 'violation of international law.' Watch US basing politics, Gulf-state diplomatic responses, and public opinion.

Treasury IRGC-asset-freeze implementation: Bessent vowed to 'economically asphyxiate this regime' — freezing IRGC offshore accounts in the British Virgin Islands and '$100 million houses… We are going to freeze those'; a 'Treasury moves to freeze IRGC assets worldwide' video item surfaces Sep 2 (MSN, unfetched). Watch for the actual freeze actions/designations and implementation details.
